newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks struggle higher at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks struggle higher at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks remained caught in a tight range Wednesday and closed modestly higher minutes after Congress mustered quorum to debate tax reforms.
"The market was waiting to see whether the lower house would get a quorum," said Jose Napoli of brokers Ignoto y Napoli. "It drifted sideways most of the session, lacking fresh buyers."
The blue-chip MerVal index erased Tuesday's slim loss to close up 0.5 percent at 547.81. Stocks pushed slightly higher in the last 10 minutes of trade, when news of the quorum reached the floor.
"A quorum pretty much guarantees approval so the markets should be relieved tomorrow," said a local investment fund manager.
The ruling Peronist bloc in the lower house failed one week ago to turn up in force, thus thwarting quorum.
Passage of the five-week-old tax package was expected to cheer investors but analysts noted the measures themselves had already been discounted.
"Even if it sails through the house I don't think the package will drive prices much higher. But it will help the markets consolidate," said the fund manager.
Technical charts show blue chips face technical resistance at between 550 and 555 points.
"The MerVal is finding it very hard to pierce that level," said Napoli. "We need new incentives to attract more volume and soak up any profit-taking."
So far this month the MerVal has climbed 7.5 percent.
In the session floor volume remained paltry at 14.5 million pesos against 13.1 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter volume shrank to 60.4 million pesos from 80.3 million Tuesday.
The broad market index matched MerVal gains of 0.5 percent, with winning issues outpacing losers 25 to 17 and 24 stocks closing flat.

Best main-tier performers were real estate developer Irsa, which jumped 2.3 percent, oil company Astra, which tacked on 1.9 percent, construction stock Juan Minetti, up 1.8 percent, and steelmaker Acindar, up 1.3 percent.
Losers were led by carmaker Sevel, sugar refiner Ledesma and agricultural holding company Cresud, which dropped 2.6 percent, 1.7 percent and 1.2 percent, respectively.
